notes.claim: In exponential change the output is multiplied by the same factor, called the growth factor, each time the input goes up by one.
A growth factor larger than one makes the quantity grow and one less than one makes it shrink.
In exponential growth the rate of growth is proportional to the current value, so growth speeds up as the amount grows.
Dividing 72 by the growth rate in percent gives the approximate doubling time (the rule of 72), a heuristic the authors suggest educators teach.
